name: Lapel Clear from Demi Guard
summary: A lapel clear from Demi Guard removes the foot-supported fabric connection while preserving top balance, returning the exchange to ordinary open guard without claiming a completed pass.
description: Lapel Clear from Demi Guard in gi BJJ: learn the starting controls, movement sequence, defensive reactions and recovery options for a connected lapel-guard exchange.
overview:
Demi uses a collar grip and foot-on-lapel support at the knee to manage forward pressure, as described by [Legion](https://legionsandiego.com/the-jiu-jitsu-dictionary/#demi-guard) and [Keenan's introduction](https://jiujitsux.com/courses/keenans-lapel-encyclopedia/lesson/16-1-introduction-to-the-demi-guard/). The top player therefore needs to address that connection while keeping base. These are conservative passing priorities inferred from the documented guard structure, not a claim to reproduce a named Demi passing lesson.

The objective here is to remove the special lapel connection and face open guard. If the bottom player recaptures one leg, recognize [[Positions/Half Guard]]; if they reverse the players, protect yourself and recover guard on landing. Driving harder into an intact connection is not equivalent to clearing it.

related_content.name: Half Guard
related_content.relationship: Retained leg trap or guard after a counter-sweep

attacker.name: Lapel Clear from Demi Guard Attacker
attacker.description: Execute Lapel Clear from Demi Guard with the right starting controls, a stable destination and a clear recovery when the attempt is blocked.
attacker.overview: You begin on top against established Demi Guard. Keep balance while removing the foot-supported lapel connection, then remove the special lapel connection and face open guard. Work only through space that is actually available; stop and release tension whenever fabric binds a knee during the change.
key_principles: Base comes before reaching to clear fabric.
Reduce the foot-supported lapel connection before driving forward.
Free the knee without twisting against the remaining wrap.
Check the leg barrier separately from the fabric grip.
Recognize the actual landing before continuing.
setup_requirements: You are in Demi Guard top, facing the bottom player.
You can identify the collar grip and foot-on-lapel connection.
Your base allows a controlled grip-clearing attempt.
You can move the knee without forcing it against tightly bound fabric.

execution_steps.description: Center your weight over a usable base before reaching for the fabric, so the reach itself does not load the opponent's elevation.
Contest the collar control without abandoning balance, reducing the pull that brings your torso over the controlled knee.
Control the accessible fabric and remove the foot's effective support, using a controlled adjustment rather than a sudden knee rotation.
Confirm that the lapel no longer binds the controlled knee before moving the leg through or away from the guard barrier.
Face the bottom player with their legs still in front, recognizing that removing the lapel has returned you to an ordinary open guard.
Check that you are balanced above open guard and the special lapel connection is gone before choosing a separate passing attack.

common_counters.counter: Restore the collar and foot connection
common_counters.your_response: Keep the remaining guard or base and reassess the controls before repeating the attempt; do not force a knee against the lapel.

common_counters.counter: Keep your knees between the torsos

common_errors.consequence: Your weight moves onto the opponent's elevation structure.
common_errors.correction: Stabilize your base before the fabric-clearing reach.

common_errors.error: Driving forward while the foot remains supported
common_errors.consequence: The same pressure can increase the bottom player's sweep opportunity.
common_errors.correction: Reduce the foot-on-lapel connection before applying passing pressure.

common_errors.error: Rotating the knee against taut fabric
common_errors.consequence: The lapel restricts the leg during the rotation.
common_errors.correction: Release the binding tension before moving the knee.

common_errors.consequence: Your passing movement stalls while one leg remains captured.
common_errors.correction: Recognize half guard and address its controls before progressing.

common_errors.error: Treating grip clearance as full positional control
common_errors.consequence: The bottom player can keep or recover ordinary guard frames.
common_errors.correction: Check fabric, legs and upper-body control as separate tasks.

training_progressions.description: You are in Demi Guard top, facing the bottom player. With a cooperative partner, identify the required grips and leg contacts, then reset without applying pressure.
Perform the listed sequence slowly with a cooperative partner. Pause at the change of lapel or foot control and reset on any joint discomfort.
Let the partner use this response: Restore the collar and foot connection. Practice keeping a safe base or guard when it blocks the attempt, then reset.
Start at the stated origin with light resistance. Stop and reset at a stable destination, a counter, or a request to release; do not continue through a bound knee.

flashcards.question: What should you establish before clearing the Demi lapel?
flashcards.answer: Establish a stable base so the act of reaching for fabric does not load the guard player's elevation structure.

flashcards.question: Why reduce the foot-on-lapel connection before driving forward?
flashcards.answer: Forward pressure into a working connection can help the bottom player elevate you instead of allowing a controlled pass.

flashcards.question: When is it safe to move the lapel-controlled knee?
flashcards.answer: Move it only after the fabric no longer binds the joint, using controlled movement and stopping on discomfort.

flashcards.question: What remains if you clear the lapel but one leg is still trapped?
flashcards.answer: The exchange has become top half guard; the remaining leg trap must be addressed before you can complete a pass.

flashcards.question: What distinguishes a lapel clear from a completed Demi pass?
flashcards.answer: A lapel clear removes the special fabric control, while a completed pass also clears both legs and establishes upper-body control from the side.

attacker.safety_considerations: Use controlled pressure with a cooperative partner when learning the lapel path. Release fabric immediately on a tap, verbal stop or discomfort. Do not rotate against a knee held by the lapel, and stop the drill when a stable landing is reached.

defender.name: Lapel Clear from Demi Guard Defender
defender.description: Recognize and respond to Lapel Clear from Demi Guard while protecting balance, remaining frames and a safe recovery route.
defender.overview: You begin underneath and are defending your Demi Guard against the passer's grip and leg clearing. Preserve the collar connection and a useful leg barrier while you still can. If the passer overcommits forward weight, the remaining structure may permit a reversal; if the lapel is lost, recover an ordinary guard promptly.
key_principles: Recognize the change of collar, lapel and foot controls early.
Keep a usable base or leg barrier while contesting the movement.
Choose a response that fits the current controls rather than a lost grip.
Release any connection that binds a knee during movement.
Identify the resulting position before continuing the exchange.
recognition_cues: The passer stabilizes their base before reaching to the fabric.
The collar grip or foot-on-tail contact is being contested.
The passer moves the knee only after reducing the fabric connection.

defensive_options.action: Restore the collar and foot connection
defensive_options.when_to_use: Before the passer has cleared the lapel from the knee
defensive_options.if_successful: You retain Demi underneath while the passer's attempt stalls.
defensive_options.risk: Reaching for lost fabric can sacrifice the leg barrier.

defensive_options.action: Keep your knees between the torsos
defensive_options.when_to_use: As the passer begins moving past the foot-on-lapel barrier
defensive_options.if_successful: You retain the starting guard by preventing the leg clearance.
defensive_options.risk: A late frame may not recover space after the passer has cleared the knees.

defensive_options.when_to_use: When the passer loses balance while the lapel connection is still working
defensive_options.if_successful: You come on top and the former passer retains half guard.
defensive_options.risk: Forcing elevation against stable base can let the passer clear the legs.

favorable_outcomes.how: Restore the collar and foot connection. You retain Demi underneath while the passer's attempt stalls.
Keep your knees between the torsos. You retain the starting guard by preventing the leg clearance.
Use forward loading to reverse. You come on top and the former passer retains half guard.

common_errors.error: Responding after the new controls are established
common_errors.consequence: The attacker completes the movement before the response affects it.
common_errors.correction: Recognize the listed cues during the control change.

common_errors.error: Turning against a knee still bound by the lapel
common_errors.consequence: The joint cannot follow the body movement freely.
common_errors.correction: Release binding tension and reset rather than forcing the turn.

common_errors.error: Ignoring the position left after the attempt
common_errors.consequence: You continue with a response intended for a guard that has already changed.
common_errors.correction: Check the actual leg and upper-body controls before the next action.

flashcards.question: What should you preserve first as the passer clears your Demi connection?
flashcards.answer: Preserve a working leg barrier and the useful collar or lapel connection, without reaching after cloth that has already been lost.

flashcards.question: Which passer mistake can supply a sweep during the lapel clear?
flashcards.answer: A forward reach that loses base can load your remaining foot-and-lapel structure and create an elevation opportunity.

flashcards.question: What should replace your lost lapel control if a leg remains reachable?
flashcards.answer: Recover an ordinary guard such as half guard around the reachable leg instead of holding ineffective fabric while being passed.

training_progressions.description: From the stated origin, have the partner begin slowly. Call out a listed recognition cue, then release and reset.
Restore the collar and foot connection. Use light resistance and stop when the response succeeds or the connection becomes uncomfortable.
Let the partner choose whether to continue or recover. Respond using the available controls; stop at the resulting stable position and name both players' roles.
